newsitem.title: USA: Michigan unemployment drops to 4.0 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: Michigan unemployment drops to 4.0 pct in May.

text.p: Michigan's seasonally adjusted unemployment rate dropped from 4.4 percent in April to a record low four percent in May, the Michigan Employment Security Agency reported Wednesday.

"After a small uptick in April, the state's unemployment rate has resumed its downward track and has now dropped by nearly a full percentage point since its 4.9 percent in January," agency acting Director Doug Stites said.
The unemployment rate for May 1996 was 4.3 percent, the agency said.
Raw unemployment numbers also dropped to the lowest level recorded in the state since April 1973, the agency said.
The state reported a gain of 15,000 jobs in May over the previous month to nearly 4.68 million.
The number of unemployed workers fell to 197,000, the lowest level since the state counted 195,000 unemployed workers in 1973, the agency said.
The figures marked the 26th consecutive month where Michigan's unemployment rate came in below the national average.
The construction industry added 3,000 jobs in May, while wholesale trade and government each contributed 2,000 new jobs, the agency said.
Manufacturing, services, and transportation, communications and utilities each added another 1,000 jobs.
Only the auto and finance, insurance and real estate industries reported job losses in May, edging down by 1,000, the agency said.
